title: Polynomial-time recognition of the 3-sphere
formal: Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm deciding whether a finite simplicial complex promised to triangulate a closed connected PL 3-manifold is PL-homeomorphic to the standard 3-sphere?
definitions: Use uniform classical deterministic Turing computation, with no advice or oracle. Integers and rational numerators and denominators are encoded in binary; L denotes the total input bit length. A polynomial bound has constants independent of the input. The complex is represented by its vertex set and list of maximal tetrahedra, with all faces implicit. The promise requires each point of its realization to have a neighborhood PL-homeomorphic to \(\mathbb{R} ^{3}\) and requires compactness, connectedness and no boundary. The standard PL 3-sphere is the boundary of a 4-simplex. PL-homeomorphism means that after finite subdivisions there is a simplicial isomorphism. Correctness is required on promised inputs; the time bound holds on all encodings.

context_blocks.text: Sphere recognition is a canonical task in computational topology. Decidability is known, but a decision algorithm can still be far too expensive as a triangulation grows.

The source places 3-sphere recognition in NP, separating certificate length from the existence of an efficient search or decision algorithm. The target is polynomial time for arbitrary promised triangulations. Results about generic triangulations or short simplifications of small examples do not settle it.

why: Determine the complexity of a basic three-dimensional topological recognition problem.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.

progress.text: The source establishes NP membership, not deterministic polynomial-time recognition.
